content: My initial prediction is **Pythium_damping_off**. Let me check the attractor guide.

No attractor guide exists for Pythium_damping_off, so my prediction stands.

The test image shows a soybean seedling just emerging from wet, dark soil. The cotyledons appear brown, water-soaked, and decayed with soil sticking to them. This is classic Pythium damping off -- the symptom description matches perfectly: "Infected seeds appear rotted with soil sticking to them; seedlings develop water-soaked lesions on the hypocotyl or cotyledons that become a brown soft rot." The wet soil conditions and soft, mushy appearance of the emerging seedling are characteristic. This differs from Rhizoctonia (which shows firm, dry, reddish-brown cankers at the soil line) and Phytophthora (which typically shows chocolate-brown stem discoloration in more developed plants).
